response.response:
No. The top FAERS reaction counts show **reporting volume, not incidence or risk**, so they cannot establish the probability of harm among all infants. The exact infant-filter coverage includes only reports with age coded in **months**, from **0 through 12 months inclusive**. Reports using other age-unit encodings are excluded. Thus, the results do **not** represent all infants. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22ibuprofen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=10)

Returned top reaction counts included vomiting (63), “off label use” (54), incorrect dose administered (48), pyrexia (44), rash (39), crying (34), diarrhoea (33), product quality issue (30), overdose (29), and accidental exposure to product (25). These remain FAERS report counts, not incidence estimates or probabilities.
